title: US and West Indies Emerge as Preferred Co-Hosts for 2034 T20 World Cup
excerpt: The ICC has confirmed dates through 2035 but no venues past 2031; a July-August 2034 window and England's withdrawal leave the 2024 co-hosts in front, The Guardian reports.
body:
• The United States and West Indies have emerged as the preferred co-hosts for the 2034 men's T20 World Cup, according to reporting by The Guardian — the ICC has not confirmed any venue beyond the 2031 World Cup.
  • The 2034 tournament is scheduled for July and August, the only men's global event in that cycle outside the autumn window, and is planned outside Asia, Africa and Oceania.
  • The two boards co-hosted the 2024 T20 World Cup, staging 16 matches in the US and 39 in the Caribbean; a 2034 split could be more even.
  • One complication: USA Cricket is suspended by the ICC over membership-rule breaches and financial irregularities, though a $3 million rescue plan has been funded.

The United States is being lined up to co-host the 2034 men's T20 World Cup with West Indies, according to a report by The Guardian carried by DailyFoxNews. The International Cricket Council announced the dates of all its global events until 2035 after its quarterly meeting in Bali last week, but has not confirmed any venues beyond the 50-over World Cup in 2031, which India and Bangladesh will host jointly.

Why the US and West Indies lead the field

All men's World Cups and the Champions Trophy in the cycle fall in the autumn except the 2034 T20 World Cup, which has been scheduled for July and August and is planned to take place outside Asia, Africa and Oceania. The England and Wales Cricket Board is understood to have ruled out a bid, as it stages the men's T20 World Cup in 2030, leaving a joint USA-West Indies event as the emerging preferred option, Cricket Addictor reported.

The ICC is keen to take major events to new markets, with the US viewed as a particularly important region as the governing body seeks to build on cricket's inclusion at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. USA Cricket and Cricket West Indies worked together on the 2024 T20 World Cup, staging 16 and 39 matches respectively, and are believed to be receptive to co-hosting again. Sources involved in preliminary planning have said a successful joint bid would likely bring a far more even allocation of matches than in 2024, as cricket in the US has developed through Major League Cricket and Olympic preparations.

"The ICC is keen to take major events to new markets, with the US viewed as a particularly important region as the governing body seeks to build on cricket's inclusion at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics."

More grounds than in 2024

USA Cricket used three grounds in 2024 — in New York, Texas and Florida. The options now also include the temporary stadium in Pomona, Southern California, that will be used for the 2028 Olympics, Frederick Cricket Park near Washington DC, Oakland Coliseum in San Francisco and Marymoor Park in Seattle, alongside the 2024 grounds at Grand Prairie in Dallas and Broward County in Florida.

In another sign of cooperation, West Indies are in discussions about playing India in two T20 internationals in North America next year, with Florida and Washington DC the most likely venues.

The complication, and what happens next

USA Cricket is suspended by the ICC due to breaches of its membership rules and financial irregularities, which resulted in the board filing for bankruptcy last year. The ICC has provided loans to assist with operational costs, and Major League Cricket's owners have funded a $3 million rescue plan, with all parties confident the matter will be resolved next year, before hosting decisions are made.

The ICC is developing its frameworks for hosting arrangements after 2031, to be completed next year, with tournaments likely to be awarded from 2028 onwards. Whether there will be a competitive tender is unclear — recent ICC tournaments have been allocated rather than contested — and would-be hosts would need to show a sound business plan, commercial viability and government guarantees. Nothing is confirmed yet: for now, the US and West Indies are the preferred option, not the appointed hosts.
